This is Rummage: a hide-and-seek game where every drawer, door and lid really opens.
The wizard has lost his manor keys, and you have to rummage through his house to find them.
We built it for the Aholo hackathon, and the whole game rests on one Lux3D feature: articulation.
For each piece, we wrote a single sentence. Lux3D turned it into a 3D model in about two minutes.
Then articulation split the model into parts, and gave each one a real joint: a drawer that slides, a door that swings, a lid that lifts.
We never rigged a hinge by hand. Every joint became a hiding spot.
Fifty-five pieces, a hundred and seven joints, five rooms, and ten levels.
On top of that, we designed the game:
padlocks that need a brass key,
At night the lights go out, and keys can hide behind paintings and under floorboards.
Hints give clues, instead of arrows.
And if you feel lucky, you can bet your time on a coin flip.
find every key, and earn your stars.
Run out of time, and the manor shows you what you missed.
You can hide a key yourself, and send the challenge to a friend.
It all runs in the browser, on desktop or phone, with nothing to install.
That's Rummage, built with Aholo Lux3D. Come and play!
